days.title: Peaks and Monastic Settlement
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Südgipfel (South Peak)
stops.detail: Skellig Michael is about 22 hectares in size, with the highest point at 217 meters on the South Peak.

stops.name: Nordgipfel
stops.detail: At almost the same height (approx. 180 m ASL), but on the neighboring North Peak, lies the small former monastic settlement, which can be reached via 618 steps of a stone staircase without railings.

stops.name: Kai
stops.detail: Boats commute daily between the mainland and Skellig Michael, allowing interested tourists to visit the monastery if weather permits, as docking and disembarking at the rocky quay is not without danger even in calm seas.

days.title: Monastic Living and Infrastructure
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: beehive huts
stops.detail: The monks lived in small cells built as stone huts (called beehive huts in Ireland) above steep cliffs using traditional Irish dry stone construction without mortar.

stops.name: Zisternen
stops.detail: The entire complex is very spartanly furnished; drinking water was collected in cisterns.

stops.name: Gartenbeete
stops.detail: On the leeward side of the rock, the monks had established small garden beds where they grew vegetables and herbs.
